name: Declared Native Consumer Recheck (native-recheck)
description: C02/C10 freshness demo: `native-bundle build` produces a real native bundle, the declared `native-recheck` route re-runs `native-bundle recheck-llvm` against it and reports equivalent; a wrong expected build id exits 1 with no claimed outcome.

harness_contract.intent: Demonstrate the C10 native consumer recheck end to end: build a real native bundle, recheck it through the declared attempt route, then show a mismatched expected build id cannot claim an outcome.
artifact_contracts: Read inputs: scenarios/native_recheck/src/main.mm (the bounded native profile atom main() -> i64 requires: true).
Step 1 builds a real mumei.native-bundle/v1 directory and saves the printed Build ID.
Step 2 runs `python -m agent native-recheck` and asserts recheck == equivalent plus a selected verifier-evidence-candidate handoff.
Step 3 flips one hex digit of the expected build id and asserts the route reports no recheck outcome, no selection, and normalized exit_code 1.
Generate evidence: build.log, recheck.log, wrong_id.log, build_id.txt, report.json, wrong_report.json, harness_state.json, result.json, and report.md.
notes: The route claims an outcome only for unambiguous exit codes: exit 1 conflates Different/UndefinedBehavior with every static failure, so a mismatched build id surfaces as no claimed outcome rather than a different label.
The produced mumei.native-consumer-evidence/v1 envelope keeps acceptance == not_evaluated: the exit code is the verdict; correspondence, producer authenticity and artifact semantics stay unassessed.
native-bundle build requires the first native profile (linux/x86_64 host, atom main() -> i64 requires: true).
Every step exits the pipe-and-grep form so a failed command cannot pass silently as exit-0 output.
budget_policy_fingerprint is native-recheck-v1 for deterministic runs.

steps.name: Build a real native bundle
steps.command: {mumei_bin} native-bundle build {root_dir}/scenarios/native_recheck/src/main.mm -o {output_dir}/bundle > {output_dir}/build.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat {output_dir}/build.log; test $rc -eq 0 && grep -o 'Build ID: [0-9a-f]*' {output_dir}/build.log | awk '{print $3}' > {output_dir}/build_id.txt && test -s {output_dir}/build_id.txt && test -f {output_dir}/bundle/native-bundle.json && test -f {output_dir}/bundle/program.ll && test -f {output_dir}/bundle/program.o && test -f {output_dir}/bundle/proof-cert.json && test -f {output_dir}/bundle/program && python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('{output_dir}/bundle/native-bundle.json')); assert d['schema']=='mumei.native-bundle/v1', d; print('schema:', d['schema']); print('native bundle built, build id saved')"
steps.artifact_contract: build.log prints a 64-hex Build ID and bundle/ holds native-bundle.json plus the four declared members (program.ll, program.o, proof-cert.json, program).
steps.verifier_gate: native-bundle build exits 0 and prints a parseable Build ID line.

steps.name: native-recheck: bundle equivalent within profile
steps.command: BUILD_ID=$(cat {output_dir}/build_id.txt); {mumei_agent_python} -m agent native-recheck --core {mumei_bin} --bundle {output_dir}/bundle --source {root_dir}/scenarios/native_recheck/src/main.mm --expected-build-id "$BUILD_ID" --output {output_dir}/report.json > {output_dir}/recheck.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat {output_dir}/report.json; cat {output_dir}/recheck.log; test $rc -eq 0 && python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('{output_dir}/report.json')); assert r['schema_version']=='mumei.native-recheck-report/v1' and r['recheck']=='equivalent' and r['sequence'].get('selected_result') is not None and r['candidate']['schema_version']=='mumei.verifier-evidence-candidate/v1', r; print('native-recheck: equivalent, candidate bound')"
steps.artifact_contract: report.json binds schema mumei.native-recheck-report/v1 with recheck == equivalent, a selected_result and a mumei.verifier-evidence-candidate/v1 candidate.
steps.verifier_gate: native-recheck exits 0, reports recheck equivalent and selects the candidate handoff.

steps.name: native-recheck: wrong expected build id claims no outcome
steps.command: BUILD_ID=$(cat {output_dir}/build_id.txt); WRONG=$(python3 -c "b='$BUILD_ID'; print(('0' if b[0] != '0' else '1') + b[1:])"); {mumei_agent_python} -m agent native-recheck --core {mumei_bin} --bundle {output_dir}/bundle --source {root_dir}/scenarios/native_recheck/src/main.mm --expected-build-id "$WRONG" --output {output_dir}/wrong_report.json > {output_dir}/wrong_id.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat {output_dir}/wrong_report.json; cat {output_dir}/wrong_id.log; test $rc -eq 0 && test "$WRONG" != "$BUILD_ID" && python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('{output_dir}/wrong_report.json')); assert 'recheck' not in r and r['normalized']['exit_code']==1 and r['sequence'].get('selected_result') is None, r; print('native-recheck: mismatched build id exits 1 with no claimed outcome')"
steps.artifact_contract: wrong_report.json carries no recheck field, normalized exit_code 1 and no selected_result for the mismatched build id.
steps.verifier_gate: native-recheck exits 0 at the route level while the mismatched build id fails with no claimed outcome and no selection.

intro: Step 1: mumei native-bundle build produces a real bundle and prints its Build ID...
Step 2: the declared native-recheck route re-runs recheck-llvm and reports equivalent...
Step 3: a mismatched expected build id cannot claim a consistent outcome...
narrative.before: A built native bundle could not be re-checked through the declared attempt boundary: the C10 consumer freshness duty stayed unassessed.
narrative.after: native-recheck re-runs recheck-llvm against the declared bundle and expected build id; matching bundles emit the three-record native-consumer-evidence envelope and a candidate handoff, while a wrong build id exits 1 with no claimed outcome.

pass.headline: Native bundle built, Build ID captured
follow_up: The bundle pins the merged IR, object, proof certificate and executable under one mumei.native-bundle/v1 record.
Step 2: Rechecking the bundle through the declared route...

pass.headline: native-recheck: equivalent + candidate bound
follow_up: The same recheck-llvm query agrees with the bundle's pinned record — the consumer-evidence envelope selects into a verifier-evidence-candidate.
Step 3: Expecting a different build id...

pass.headline: Mismatched build id exits 1, no claimed outcome
follow_up: Exit 1 conflates Different with every static failure — the route claims no outcome and selects nothing.
Demo complete: the C10 native consumer recheck boundary is observable end to end.
